subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - pricing & capacity follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T18:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - pricing & capacity follow-up

Alex — great talking earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned on requirements for a Dedicated capacity quote: 

Summary of what you shared (please correct if I missed anything):
- Expected steady-state usage: ~50M tokens/month initially; planning to scale to ~500M tokens/month within 6 months.
- Peak day: up to ~100M tokens/day during product launch windows.
- Typical prompt+generation length: ~150 tokens average, with some longer generations up to ~800 tokens.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 350 ms for user-facing chat flows.
- Target throughput: support ~200 concurrent users with ~1 request/sec each (approx ~30k reqs/day), translating to ~8-10k tokens/sec at peak bursts (workload is bursty).
- Budget: steering range $10k-40k/month for inference and infra; target unit economics around $8-12 per 1M tokens initially.

Questions we need to confirm before we put together the Dedicated quote:
1) Model family and size you plan to run on Dedicated (tight coupling to GPU selection): open to using an Llama-variant ~30B or do you need 70B / mix of both?
2) Do you expect real-time KV cache reuse across sessions (chat history reuse) or mostly fresh prompts? This impacts memory and throughput requirements.
3) Any regulatory constraints that require Private deployment (VPC) or is Dedicated in our shared control plane acceptable?

Initial recommendation (internal, subject to confirmation):
- If you run ~30B-class models primarily: 2-4 x NVIDIA A10G can be a cost-efficient starting point for bursty chat; A10G gives strong throughput for 30B and is more cost-effective.
- If you plan to use 70B-class models or need highest latency/throughput: 2-3 x A100 80GB nodes (or 1-2 reserved proportionally larger instances) to meet 95p <350ms and support KV caching.
- Reserved capacity sizing: start with a 2 GPU pool (A10G) with ability to burst to 4 during launch windows; typical monthly committed seats for this profile land in the $12k-25k/month range depending on model and commitment term.

Next steps / action items:
- Alex: confirm model size (30B vs 70B) and whether KV cache reuse will be high. Also share a one-week sample traffic CSV if possible (I attached a template).
- Marcus/Dylan: I'll loop you to validate throughput targets and convert to an internal capacity quote (GPU selection, reserved sizing, expected tokens/$ metrics).
- We'll run a quick cost-per-1M-tokens estimate once Alex confirms model and sample traffic; aim to hit Alex's target $8-12 / 1M tokens.

I attached a traffic_breakdown.csv template and a draft SOW for your procurement team to review. I'll follow up with a formal capacity quote by EOD tomorrow after Marcus validates the throughput assumptions.

Thanks — Marissa

--

Thanks Marissa — this aligns well. A few clarifications: 
- Model plan: start with a 30B open LLM for chat (production), keep 70B for a small set of high-quality responses that can be offloaded to hosted endpoints if needed. So hybrid is likely.
- KV reuse: yes, heavy cache reuse within sessions (we keep context ~3-6 turns).
- Traffic: I attached a quick export (traffic_breakdown.csv) showing weekday peaks that map to ~80M tokens/day on peak launch days and ~45M tokens/day normal. Monthly is ~60M tokens/month today, expecting 10x in 6 months.
- Budget: our procurement band is flexible but we're targeting $20k/month commit for H1, want to understand how that maps to reserved GPUs and whether it meets latency SLOs.

Please proceed with a 2x A10G and 2x A100 scenario in the quote (we'd like both cost and perf tradeoffs). Also include a best-effort $/1M token estimate for both.

Appreciate it — Alex

--

Looping in my throughput notes after reviewing Alex's CSV and your recap: 
- Given heavy KV reuse and 30B as primary model, A10G pool is reasonable for steady-state. We can expect ~700-900 tokens/sec per A10G for optimized 30B runtimes with our runtime optimizations and batching. That translates to ~60-80M tokens/day sustained per GPU under ideal batching and caching.
- For burst windows (peak day ~80-100M tokens/day), we should size for 2x A10G baseline and ability to burst to 4x A10G. That will keep 95p latency under 350 ms for most chat flows.
- 70B traffic (small subset) should be routed to 1x A100 80GB reserved or use hosted fallback for cost control. For strict latency and throughput on 70B, an A100 will provide ~200-300 tokens/sec for 70B depending on sequence length; if they need 70B for more than 10% of traffic we should consider adding a second A100.

Cost / unit economics roughs (ballpark for discussion):
- 2x A10G reserved pool: estimated committed price ~$11k-~$15k/month (depends on term). Effective $/1M tokens (assuming 60M tokens/month sustained) ~ $12-~$18 / 1M tokens.
- 2x A10G + 1x A100 baseline: ~$18k-~$25k/month; effective $/1M tokens improves at scale (if they hit 200M+ tokens/month) to ~$6-~$10 / 1M tokens.

I'll prepare a formal spreadsheet (capacity_quote.xlsx) with per-GPU throughput estimates, expected tokens/day capacity, and a couple of pricing tiers (monthly commit vs annual discount).

-Marcus

Alex — thanks for the fast responses and the CSV. Attached is the initial capacity_quote.xlsx and a draft SOW; the sheet shows two scenarios per Marcus' notes:

Scenario A (cost-first, 30B primary):
- Baseline: 2x A10G reserved
- Burst: up to 4x A10G (autoscale/burst policy)
- Monthly commit estimate: $13k/month (12-month term reduces to ~$11k/mo)
- Estimated $/1M tokens: $12-~$15 at current volumes; improves with utilization

Scenario B (performance-first, hybrid 30B + 70B):
- Baseline: 2x A10G + 1x A100 80GB reserved
- Burst: 4x A10G + option to add 2nd A100 for sustained 70B traffic
- Monthly commit estimate: $20k-~$25k/month (term-dependent)
- Estimated $/1M tokens: $6-~$10 at scale (200M+ tokens/month)

Action items: 
- Alex: confirm which scenario you want priced for a formal quote and whether procurement will commit to a 12-month or quarterly term.
- Alex: sign off on the draft SOW or send any edits to procurement@finlytics.com.
- Marcus: finalize the spreadsheet and I'll turn this into a formal proposal and send it to Alex by EOD (includes DocuSign link).

If this looks good I'll prepare a DocuSign package and include estimated burn-rate charts tied to tokens/month so procurement can visualize unit economics vs usage.

Best — Marissa
